Chow Test (structural break), scale-aware re-implementation

Source: R/hcp_chow.R
hcp_chow.Rd

Change-point detection by structural break in a linear model. This is a native re-implementation (no strucchange dependency) and an adaptation of the original Chow/strucchange approach with a documented innovation: where the classical Chow test only compares the mean regression coefficients of the two sub-samples (homoskedastic errors), this version reports the single break that maximises the Gaussian mean + variance log-likelihood ratio over an unknown break date. It is therefore scale-aware – it also detects variance/scale regime changes the mean-only Chow test is blind to. The break is scanned over the trimmed range following the sup-type construction of Andrews (1993).

This mirrors the canonical implementation in the pyharbinger package (class HcpChow); the two implementations produce identical detections.

Usage

hcp_chow()

Value

hcp_chow object

References

  • Chow GC (1960). Tests of equality between sets of coefficients in two linear regressions. Econometrica, 28(3):591-605.

  • Andrews DWK (1993). Tests for parameter instability and structural change with unknown change point. Econometrica, 61(4):821-856.

  • Chen J, Gupta AK (2000). Parametric Statistical Change Point Analysis. Birkhauser. (Gaussian mean+variance change points)

  • Zeileis A, Leisch F, Hornik K, Kleiber C (2002). strucchange: An R package for testing for structural change in linear regression models. Journal of Statistical Software, 7(2). doi:10.18637/jss.v007.i02 (original approach)

Examples

library(daltoolbox)

# Load change-point example data
data(examples_changepoints)

# Use a simple example
dataset <- examples_changepoints$simple
head(dataset)
#>   serie event
#> 1  0.00 FALSE
#> 2  0.25 FALSE
#> 3  0.50 FALSE
#> 4  0.75 FALSE
#> 5  1.00 FALSE
#> 6  1.25 FALSE

# Configure the Chow detector
model <- hcp_chow()

# Fit the detector (no-op for Chow)
model <- fit(model, dataset$serie)

# Run detection
detection <- detect(model, dataset$serie)

# Show detected change points
print(detection[(detection$event),])
#>    idx event        type
#> 49  49  TRUE changepoint
